title: What is the area of this fraction rectangle?
description: A rectangle with sides one half and one quarter of a unit sits inside a unit square, and the video finds its area by counting how many such rectangles fill the square. Keeko then raises a hand with the doubt that the area is found by adding the two sides.
teaching_notes: One idea: the area of a rectangle with fraction sides equals the product of its sides. Watch for students who add the two sides to get the area.

source: In the unit square, a shaded rectangle has sides 1/2 unit and 1/4 unit, and 8 such rectangles fill the square. What is its area, and how does it relate to the sides?
video_script.why: The child has cut a quarter into two equal parts in a unit square and now sees the same picture as the area of a rectangle.
video_script.substitution: Eight equal rectangles fill a square of area one square unit, so one rectangle has one eighth of a square unit, and its sides multiply to the same number.
video_script.anchor: A rectangle with sides one half and one quarter of a unit sits in a unit square: what is its area?
video_script.wrong_move: adds the two sides, one half and one quarter, and gets three quarters, though eight such rectangles would then be much larger than the whole square
video_script.payoff_line: The area is one eighth of a square unit, and it equals one half times one quarter

final_answer.spoken: one eighth of a square unit, which equals one half times one quarter

video_script.fraction_reading: one half, one quarter, one eighth, three quarters
maths_rules: 8 rectangles fill the square, so one rectangle = 1 ÷ 8 = 1/8 square unit
sides 1/2 unit and 1/4 unit cut the square into 2 × 4 = 8 equal parts
the slip: 1/2 + 1/4 = 3/4, and 8 × 3/4 = 6 square units, far more than 1
video_script.design: One idea: the area of a rectangle with fraction sides equals the product of its sides. The unit square with the shaded rectangle is the anchor and stays all video; the working band builds in the idea part.

marks.rule: the two sides multiply and the area 1/8 returns

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks the area is three quarters of a square unit.
Keeko added the two sides.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>But eight rectangles of that area would be much more than the whole square.
The whole square has an area of only one square unit.
<bookmark mark='rule'/>The area is found by multiplying the two sides, and not by adding them.
